title: AMD Q3 2026 Earnings Data Center Growth Drives Record Quarter
gist: AMD's Q3 2026 revenue was $13.377B (+45% YoY), led by Data Center at $8.546B (+97% YoY) on EPYC and Instinct MI450; Q4 guidance of about $17B implies further acceleration. The author expects x86 leadership with Venice versus Intel's later Diamond Rapids.

themes.theme: AMD Q3 results and Q4 guide

insights.claim: AMD's Q3 2026 revenue reached $13.377 billion, up 45% year over year and 16% sequentially, with non-GAAP EPS of $2.09 and GAAP EPS of $1.46.
insights.speaker: Cliff Robinson
insights.so_what: Sets the baseline for a step-change quarter in AMD's AI/server business.

insights.claim: AMD guides Q4 2026 revenue to about $17 billion plus or minus 3%, roughly 66% YoY and 27% sequential growth at the midpoint, implying acceleration beyond Q3.
insights.speaker: Cliff Robinson
insights.so_what: Guide implies another large step up; sets the bar for Q4 expectations.
insights.quote: AMD expects fourth-quarter 2026 revenue of approximately $17 billion plus or minus 3%.
insights.locator: AMD Q4 Guidance Points To Acceleration

insights.claim: Non-GAAP operating income was $3.923B versus GAAP operating income of $2.832B on the same revenue, a gap of about $1.1B from stock comp and acquisition amortization.
insights.speaker: Cliff Robinson
insights.so_what: Quality-of-earnings gap between GAAP and non-GAAP is sizable.

insights.claim: AMD Data Center revenue hit $8.546B, up 97% YoY and 27% sequentially, attributed to strong EPYC demand and the launch of Instinct MI450 GPUs.
insights.speaker: Cliff Robinson
insights.so_what: Data Center is now about 64% of AMD revenue, driving the equity story.

insights.claim: AMD says Anthropic, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI and Oracle Cloud Infrastructure are running workloads on Helios rack-scale solutions powered by its chips, giving AMD a broad AI-lab customer list.
insights.speaker: Cliff Robinson
insights.so_what: Customer breadth validates AMD as a credible second source to Nvidia at rack scale.

insights.claim: AMD's Data Center segment (97% YoY growth) is growing faster than Intel's data center business ($7.3B, up 78% YoY), and AMD appears to be accelerating while both benefit from AI and server CPU demand.
insights.speaker: Cliff Robinson
insights.so_what: Share shift toward AMD continues in the datacenter.
insights.quote: AMD’s Data Center segment at $8.546 billion grew faster at 97%.
insights.locator: AMD’s Data Center Is Big Time

insights.claim: The author expects AMD to hold clear x86 performance leadership with Venice, since Intel's PCIe Gen6 Diamond Rapids platform is expected later in 2027, and thinks AMD is managing supply better to get chips out.
insights.speaker: Cliff Robinson
insights.so_what: A time window of x86 leadership could support server CPU share and pricing for AMD.

insights.claim: Venice is a major platform update (more DDR5 channels and PCIe Gen6), so PCIe Gen6 development will likely happen more often on AMD than on Intel, as with PCIe Gen4.
insights.speaker: Cliff Robinson
insights.so_what: Ecosystem Gen6 validation and early adoption may skew toward AMD platforms.

insights.claim: It remains an open question how large a price premium AMD can extract for its generational advantage and first-mover status with Venice.
insights.speaker: Cliff Robinson
insights.so_what: Pricing power on server CPUs is a key margin variable.

insights.claim: AMD's combined Client and Gaming segment fell 8% YoY to $3.722B, with client up slightly and gaming down; memory and NAND prices are keeping a lid on the market.
insights.speaker: Cliff Robinson
insights.so_what: Memory/NAND cost inflation is a headwind for PC and console demand.

insights.claim: AMD highlighted three AI-related client products while Intel's client segment bullets focused on shortages, future-product demand and a generic AI PC nod; the author wonders whether Strix Halo's ability to run reasonably large models locally is a driver.
insights.speaker: Cliff Robinson
insights.so_what: Local-LLM-capable client silicon may be a differentiator for AMD in PCs.

insights.claim: AMD's Embedded segment earned $1.109B, up 29% YoY, driven by aerospace and defense, automotive, communications and industrial; the author says it offsets client and gaming weakness.
insights.speaker: Cliff Robinson
insights.so_what: Xilinx-era embedded business has grown to a scale rivaling Xilinx's entire annual revenue at acquisition (about $3.1-3.2B) on an annualized basis.
